page.layout: One printed page, no margin notes. Top: page number 154 at upper left, running head "Præterit. Plusq. perfect." centred above text. Body: a verb paradigm with a bracket grouping the Latin forms beside German glosses in two columns, then headings and lines of conjugation below. Foot: catchword "Futur." at lower right.

main_text.p: Ich hatte, du hattest, er hatte, wir hatten, jhr hattet, sie hatten gehabt.
main_text.head: Futurum,
main_text.p: Io hauerò, hauro & haro, Ego habebo, ich werd haben. (haben.
Tu hauerai, haurai & harai. Tu habebis, du wirst
Colui haurà, haurà & harà, ille habebit, er wird haben.
Noi haueremo, hauremo, & haremo, nos habebi-mus. Wir werden haben.
Voi hauerete, & haurete, & harete, vos habebitis, Ihr werdet haben.
Coloro haueranno, hauranno, & haranno, illi habebunt, sie werden haben.
main_text.head: Imperatiuo modo temp. praf.
main_text.p: Habbi tu, habe tu, habe du.
Habbi colui, habeat ille, habe er.
Habbiamo noi, habeamus nos, haben wir.
Habbiate voi, habete vos, habet jhr.
Habbiano coloro, habeant illi, haben sie.

page.notes: Bracket grouping ("hauuto") is a printed brace; the Latin forms of the pluperfect were printed in two columns. Some lines are hard to read at the edge of the scan and were transcribed as best as possible. Catchword "Futur." lies at the lower right.
